open_points.subject: minted entity identifiers
open_points.text: `trial_execution_id` M07, `binding_id` M11, `run_id` M19, `approval_id` M24 and `grant_id` M25 are minted at random by the kernel; one that already exists is minted again.
open_points.question: Which module or capability owns the random source, identifier encoding, and collision check used by the several record-owning modules?
options: Each record-owning module mints and checks its own identifiers
The store provides one identifier-minting capability
A separate kernel randomness/identity provider owns minting
open_points.default_guess: Have the store provide one collision-checked identifier-minting capability.

open_points.subject: installed-instance startup validation
open_points.text: for one it also selects an instance for, a manifest record that cannot be read or fails a check of the record itself (A08 rule 5) stops the start naming it
open_points.question: Which capability entry or entries are checked at startup, and which exact A08 rule 5 checks count as checks of the record itself when no operation or proposal ports have been named?
options: Check only service-level structure and the selected instance facts needed for header collision detection
Check every capability entry using only checks independent of proposal ports
Do not validate capabilities at startup beyond reading the selected instance's required headers
open_points.default_guess: Check only service-level structure and the selected instance facts required for the credential-header collision check.

open_points.subject: advancement of waiting elements
open_points.text: A waiting element can still execute, so M19's "no node can run any more" holds only when nothing waits; Elements waiting on approval or an unknown outcome are not touched.
open_points.question: Can a waiting element execute during ordinary run advancement, or can it move only through its designated approve, resume, or resolve operation?
options: Waiting elements move only through approve, resume, or resolve as appropriate
Waiting elements may be selected by ordinary advancement
Only service-unreachable elements may be selected again during ordinary advancement
open_points.default_guess: Waiting elements move only through the explicit operation appropriate to their waiting reason.
